assessment.nobel_worthiness: Established, in physical terms, how electrons tunnel over long distances through protein matrices, with distance and driving-force dependences measured by time-resolved kinetics in ruthenium-modified proteins. It is the quantitative backbone for understanding respiratory and photosynthetic electron transfer, close to the physical-mechanism standard I apply to biological energy conversion.
assessment.attribution: The credited set is two people, so it fits the three-laureate limit with no trimming. Gray and Winkler are the long-standing core of the experimental program; the theoretical framework (Marcus, already recognized, and Hopfield and Beratan-Onuchic style tunneling-pathway models) is separate and would need clear explanation in the citation.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation and wide adoption in bioenergetics; the interpretation is stable and recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would see the work as an extension of Marcus-theory recognition rather than a distinct discovery.
I am recalling the history of the tunneling-pathway models and cannot independently verify the allocation of priority among theorists.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase is a central enzyme of the nitrogen cycle, and the structures of the FeMo-cofactor, including the interstitial carbide and the turnover intermediates with bound ligands, together with the kinetic and spectroscopic work on electron and proton delivery, address a fundamental chemical mechanism in a living system. It is the kind of biochemistry and biophysics where structure and time-resolved chemistry have to be read together.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread over structure (Rees, Einsle, and others), biochemical genetics and cofactor biosynthesis (Dean, Ribbe), and mechanistic kinetics (Seefeldt). This is a candidacy resting on a line of work, and a three-person split would leave out meaningful contributors. I propose the structural and mechanistic core.
assessment.maturity: The structural picture is well confirmed by independent groups; the catalytic mechanism at the atomic level is still debated, so the field is only partly mature.
uncertainties: The identity and sequence of intermediates in the Lowe-Thorneley cycle are not settled.
Allocation among structure, biosynthesis and mechanism is unresolved, and the expert reports would need to weigh it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers enables diffraction-before-destruction structures of microcrystals and time-resolved structural movies of reactions, including photoactive and light-driven enzymes. This is a method that makes dynamic mechanisms visible, which I weigh heavily.
assessment.attribution: The founding proof of principle involved a larger group (Chapman, Fromme, Spence, Hajdu, Schlichting and others). Chapman led the method, Fromme the membrane protein crystallography, and Schlichting the time-resolved enzymology; Hajdu's early conceptual role is a competing claim. The three-person limit forces a hard choice.
assessment.maturity: Roughly fifteen years of use, with growing reproducible time-resolved results; some benefit over cryo-EM and synchrotron methods remains narrow, so timing is reasonable but not urgent.
uncertainties: Priority among Hajdu, Chapman and Spence, which I cannot verify.
Dependence on a handful of large facilities limits breadth of impact so far.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer is the physical principle behind proton pumping, water oxidation and many redox enzymes. Concerted and stepwise pathways, the role of hydrogen bonding and the vibronic theory give a unified framework that bears directly on how respiratory enzymes work.
assessment.attribution: Meyer introduced the early concept and molecular systems, Mayer developed bond-dissociation free energy and concerted proton-electron transfer, Hammes-Schiffer supplied the theory, and Nocera the electrocatalysis and the model for the photosystem. Four credited names for three seats makes the allocation contestable.
assessment.maturity: The framework is accepted and widely used; the experimental discrimination of mechanisms in enzymes is still moving.
uncertainties: Diffuse attribution among concept, theory and catalysis.
Distance between the model-complex work and the enzyme systems it is meant to explain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hijacking the ubiquitin-proteasome system with small molecules to remove a chosen protein created a new modality, and the mechanistic discovery that thalidomide-type drugs act through cereblon unified it with molecular glues. The chemistry and the clinical consequences are substantial.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies launched PROTACs, Ciulli made the ligands and structural basis for VHL-recruiting degraders, and Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the thalidomide target. Allocation among PROTACs and glues, and among the many credited names, is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Clinical trials are under way but approvals of degraders are limited, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Whether clinical validation is sufficient for the committee.
Whether PROTACs and molecular glues should be one prize or are separate discoveries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The energy-landscape and funnel view of protein folding resolves Levinthal's paradox in physical terms and links statistical mechanics to kinetics, with experiments mapping folding transition states.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic are the central theorists with Bryngelson, and Dill proposed related ideas; Fersht provides the experimental protein-engineering approach. The split between theory and experiment weakens a single clean citation.
assessment.maturity: The concept is long established and widely accepted, and later prediction of structure by machine learning has changed the context, which complicates how the discovery would be framed.
uncertainties: Overlap with recent recognition of protein structure prediction.
Priority among Bryngelson, Dill, Wolynes and Onuchic.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cryo-EM structures of spliceosome states reveal how the RNA-protein machine catalyzes two transesterification steps, giving a mechanistic picture for a central biochemical process. This is a structural result that makes dynamics visible.
assessment.attribution: Lührmann's biochemical dissection and the cryo-EM structures from the Lührmann/Stark and Shi laboratories are the core; Nguyen and others contributed later structures. Structure alone would not credit the earlier genetic and biochemical work on splicing recognized in 1993.
assessment.maturity: The structures are confirmed by several groups, though the full mechanism of dynamic remodeling is incomplete.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier splicing recognition in medicine and chemistry.
Whether a field of structures rather than one discovery is being rewarded.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as a principle of cellular organization has changed how condensates and membraneless organelles are thought of, bringing polymer physics to cell biology.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman made the key cellular observation on P granules, and Rosen provided the multivalent-interaction biochemistry; Pappu and Mittag are credited for theory and sequence grammar. Not all of these fit three seats.
assessment.maturity: The concept is young and still contested regarding physiological significance and how to distinguish condensates from aggregation.
uncertainties: Premature if the biological relevance remains disputed.
The molecular mechanisms are less established than a physical-mechanism standard demands.
